# TypeScript SDK

The functions a film imports from `"turbomotion"`, taken from the doc comments on the exports in `crates/script/sdk`. Only documented exports are listed. Blocks marked `ts example` are whole film scripts: save one as `film.ts` and `turbomotion sdk build film.ts` builds it (a test builds and checks every one).

## `arg-check`

Checks on the positional arguments of the layer builders, so a wrong guess names the right form where it was written instead of surfacing as an engine schema error about a property the author never typed.

```ts
export function show(v: unknown): string
```
What was passed, short enough for a message.

```ts
export function checkSolidColor(color: unknown): asserts color is Color
```
`solid("#101828")`: the colour is the first argument, not an option.

```ts
export function checkTextContent(content: unknown): void
```
`text("Hello", opts)` or `text({ from: 0, to: 100 }, opts)`: the words (or a counter or swap) come first.

```ts
export function checkRectSize(w: unknown, h: unknown): void
```
`rect(260, 340, opts)`: width and height in pixels.

```ts
export function checkGroupOpts(o: unknown): void
```
`group(opts, children)`: options first, then the layers that follow it.

```ts
export function checkLayerKeys(kind: string, id: string, keys: string[]): void
```
Every key of a layer must be one the engine reads for that type; the engine itself says which (and the nearest valid name).

```ts
export function checkTextureShader(shader: unknown): void
```
`texture("noise", opts)`: the generator's name is the first argument, not an option.

```ts
export const LAYER_STATE = ["id", "props", "tweens", "children"];
```
Layer properties a script may still assign after construction: the builder's own state (everything else is written by \`set\`).

```ts
export function refuseLayerAssignment(kind: string, id: string, key: string): never
```
\`layer.effects = [...]\` writes nowhere: a layer's options are the engine's keys, in \`props\`. Name the place that works.

## `assets`

Artwork from code: SVG through the engine's importer (`svg`, `svgFile`) and pixel art from rows of characters.

```ts
export function svg(source: string, o: SvgOpts = {}): Layer
```
SVG markup (`"<svg ...>"`) or bare path data (`"M0 0 L10 0 ..."`) as a shape layer; its `anchor` is the artwork's centre.

```ts example
import { comp, svg } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(svg("<svg viewBox='0 0 10 10'><path d='M5 0 L10 10 L0 10 Z' fill='#ffd166'/></svg>", { id: "triangle", width: 400, pos: [960, 540] }));
export default film;
```

```ts
export function svgFile(path: string, o: SvgOpts = {}): Layer
```
An `.svg` file next to the film (or under its `root`), imported like `svg()`. The file is watched by `sdk watch`.

```ts
export function pixelSprite(rows: string[], palette: Record<string, Color>, o: PixelOpts = {}): Layer
```
Pixel art from rows of characters: `pixelSprite(["..aa..", ".aaaa."], { a: "#ff5a1f" }, { px: 6 })`. `.` and space are clear; centred on its position.

```ts example
import { comp, pixelSprite } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(pixelSprite(
  ["..aa..", ".aaaa.", "aabbaa", "aaaaaa", ".a..a."],
  { a: "#ff5a1f", b: "#ffffff" },
  { id: "invader", px: 40, pos: [960, 540] },
));
export default film;
```

## `blend-types`

The layer blend modes (crates/core/src/effects/blend/table.rs): the engine's own names, in its order, then its aliases. `docs/reference/blend-modes.md` says what each one does; a test fails when this list and the engine's differ.

```ts
export type BlendMode =
```
How a layer combines with what is below it. `"linear_dodge"` is another name for `"add"`.

## `comp`

The film: size, frame rate, layers, and the edit timeline of shots, transitions, overlays and hits.

```ts
export class Shot
```
A shot of the edit timeline, built by `shot()`.

```ts
export const shot = (opts: ShotOpts): Shot
```
One shot of the edit: its layers, how it comes in (`in`), a 2D `move`, a 3D `camera` move.

```ts example
import { comp, shot, text } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, bg: "#1a1d29" });
const title = (id: string, words: string) => text(words, { id, size: 160, weight: 800, color: "#ffffff", align: "center", pos: [960, 540] });
film.timeline({
  shots: [
    shot({ id: "one", dur: 1.5, layers: [title("one-title", "One")], move: "push_in" }),
    shot({ id: "two", dur: 1.5, layers: [title("two-title", "Two")], in: { type: "push_left", dur: 0.4 } }),
  ],
});
export default film;
```

```ts
export class Film
```
A composition being built: add layers, shots, audio and markers, and it becomes the JSON the engine renders.

```ts
export const comp = (opts: CompOpts): Film
```
The film: `comp({ width, height, fps, bg, ... })`, then `film.add(layers)`, `film.shot(...)` and `export default film`.

```ts example
import { comp, text } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(text("A film", { id: "title", size: 160, weight: 800, color: "#ffffff", align: "center", pos: [960, 540] }));
export default film;
```

## `compile`

Turns the tweens a timeline recorded on a layer into the engine's property forms. Timeline positions are in the clock the layer lives in (shot time, or comp time); the engine reads a layer's keys from the layer's own `start`, so every time written out is shifted by that start here, and nowhere else.

```ts
export type LayerTime = (t: number)
```
Converts a time on the timeline's clock to the layer's own time.

```ts
export function layerTime(out: Record<string, any>, tweens: Tween[], id: string): LayerTime
```
The layer's `start` as a number; tweens cannot be placed against a start the SDK cannot read.

```ts
export function compileTweens(out: Record<string, any>, all: Tween[], id: string): void
```
Write the tweens of one layer into `out` (the layer's JSON): one merged property per animated name.

## `components/appear`

An entrance for a whole component: every visible layer enters with an engine preset ("fade", "slide_up", "pop", ...), optionally one after another. It uses the layers' own `enter`, so it never fights the animation a component already has.

```ts
export type AppearPreset = "fade" | "slide_up" | "slide_down" | "slide_left" | "slide_right" | "pop" | "zoom_in" | "zoom_out" | "blur" | "whip_left" | "whip_right" | "spin";
```
The presets of `comp catalogue` that make sense as an entrance.

```ts
export type AppearOpt = AppearPreset | AppearSpec;
```
A preset name, or the full spec.

```ts
export function appear(layers: Layer[] | Part, opt: AppearOpt, at: number): number
```
Make `layers` enter from `at`. Groups (null layers) are skipped: their children enter themselves. Returns when the last one is in.

```ts
export function entrance<T extends Part>(part: T, opt: AppearOpt | undefined, at: number): T
```
What a component does last: add its entrance (when asked for) and report the later `end`.

## `components/barRace`

Horizontal bars that grow to their values, each with a label on the left and a counter riding its tip.

```ts
export function barRace(o: BarRaceOpts): Part
```
`barRace({ tl, at: 37, dur: 2.4, bars: [{ label: "turbomotion", value: 373, color: "#ff5a1f" }, ...] })`.

## `components/bboxOverlay`

HUD bounding boxes with mono labels (`name · 1240×180 · ok`). A box has a state (ok / clash / fixed) shown in a token colour, and may change state and move at a later time (a clash that is fixed).

```ts
export const stateColor = (th: Theme, s: BoxState): string
```
Box colours: ok = cobalt, clash = turbo (the red of this palette), fixed = volt.

```ts
export function bboxOverlay(o: BboxOverlayOpts): Part
```
`bboxOverlay({ tl, at: 1, boxes: [{ x: 120, y: 80, w: 1240, h: 180, label: "title" }] })`; `x`,`y` are the top-left.

## `components/blob`

An organic blob: a smooth closed outline with seeded wobble, optionally morphing into a second blob (and back).

```ts
export function blobPath(points: number, r: number, wobble: number, seed: number): string
```
A smooth closed path of `points` lobes around radius `r`; the same `points` always give a path the engine can morph between.

```ts
export function blob(o: BlobOpts): BlobPart
```
`blob({ id: "b", size: 320, seed: 4, fill: "#3D6BFF", pos: [960, 540], morph: { tl, seed: 9, at: 1, dur: 1.2, back: true } })`.

## `components/browserWindow`

A generic browser window: three dots, a URL pill, a spinner and a skeleton page. No real brand marks.

```ts
export function browserWindow(o: BrowserWindowOpts): Part
```
`browserWindow({ tl, url: "localhost:3000", at: 0.4 })`: `root` is the group to move or break apart.

## `components/capsule`

A pill: two round ends joined by straight sides. Shape items turn about the layer origin, not their own centre, so capsules at an angle are built as paths.

```ts
export function capsulePath(x: number, y: number, len: number, w: number, deg: number): string
```
SVG path of a capsule `len` long and `w` wide, starting at (x, y) and pointing `deg` degrees clockwise from +x.

```ts
export function capsule(o: CapsuleOpts): Layer
```
`capsule({ w: 40, len: 200, deg: 30, fill: "#3D6BFF", pos: [400, 300] })`, or `capsule({ from: [100, 100], to: [500, 300], w: 24, fill })`.

## `components/cardWall`

A tilted wall of coloured 3D cards that pops in from the centre, with a hero card the camera can dolly toward. The wall's origin is the hero card, so a camera aimed at the wall is aimed at the hero.

```ts
export function cardWall(o: CardWallOpts): Part
```
`cardWall({ tl, cols: 8, rows: 5, seed: 11, hero: 20, at: 0.1 })`: `wall` is the parent, `hero` the hero card layer.

## `components/codePanel`

A mono code panel: syntax colours (as text `runs`), a highlight bar that moves to the current line, and lines that are typed or revealed one per `perLine` seconds with a `tick` each.

```ts
export function highlight(line: string, c: Record<string, string>): TextRun[]
```
Syntax `runs` for one line of TypeScript-like code.

```ts
export function codePanel(o: CodePanelOpts): Part
```
`codePanel({ tl, at: 12.5, perLine: 1, lines: ["const film = comp({ ... });", ...] })`.

## `components/cube`

Cubes made of 3D shape faces: a solid cube with its own art on each face, a 3x3x3 puzzle cube whose slabs twist, and a tile that flips from art to a letter. Every function returns `{ root, layers, ... }`: put `layers` straight into a shot and move, spin or scale `root`.

```ts
export interface CubeFace { fill?: Color; items?: Items }
```
One face: a fill, and shape items drawn on it (centred on the face, in pixels).

```ts
export function cube(o: CubeOpts): CubePart
```
`cube({ id: "c", size: 200, faces: ["#3D6BFF", { fill: "#FF5A1F", items: icon }] , pos: [960, 540, 0] })`.

```ts
export function puzzleCube(o: PuzzleCubeOpts): PuzzleCubePart
```
A 3x3x3 puzzle cube: three slabs you can twist, each tile its own colour and art.

```ts
export function letterCube(o: LetterCubeOpts): CubePart
```
A tile that flips from art (front) to a letter (back): rotate `root` 180 about y.

## `components/cutout`

A cut-out subject that is alive: a picture (or any layer) standing on the ground with a contact shadow, moving by itself. Idle motion is a looping expression on the *body*, so the group around it stays free for the film's own moves (a stage glides the group between poses, a timeline enters it) and the two never fight over one property.  const hand = cutout({ id: "hand", src: "assets/hand.png", size: [300, 290], pivot: "base", idle: { float: { amp: 12, period: 3.2 }, sway: { deg: 3, period: 4.1 } }, shadow: { width: 260, y: 150 }, ring: { rx: 230 } }); shot({ layers: [hand] });                 // pos, scale, rotation and opacity of `hand.root` are yours to move

```ts
export interface Wave
```
A looping wave: one full cycle every `period` seconds, offset by `phase` (0..1 of a cycle).

```ts
export interface CutoutOpts
```
Options for `cutout`: an image or built layer that lives by itself (float, sway, breathe, drift, tilt).

```ts
export function cutout(o: CutoutOpts): Part
```
`cutout({ id, src, size, idle, shadow, ring })`: `root` is the group to place and move; `body` is the picture.

## `components/dollyZoom`

The vertigo shot: the camera travels while its lens zooms the other way, so the subject plane stays the same size and the depth behind it stretches.

```ts
export function dollyZoom(cam: Layer, o: DollyZoomOpts): number
```
`dollyZoom(cam, { tl, at: 0.5, dur: 2, amount: 0.4 })`. Give the camera `pos: [cx, cy, -distance]` and `zoom: distance` first. Returns the end time.

A two-sided card in 3D: it turns over to show its back. Each side is a fill, shape items and an optional label.

```ts
export function flipTile(o: FlipTileOpts): FlipTilePart
```

`flipTile({ tl, id: "t", size: 240, pos: [960, 540], front: { fill: "#3D6BFF", label: "?" }, back: { fill: "#C8F031", label: "A" }, at: 1 })`.

A frosted-glass panel: a soft shadow, a translucent body with a sheen, and a bright rim. The `backdrop` effect blurs whatever is already composited behind the panel body.

`glassPanel({ id: "card", pos: [960, 540], size: [640, 360], radius: 28, tint: "#cfe1ff" })`.

A stylised glowing hand (vector artwork): forearm, palm, four fanned fingers and a thumb, pointing along +x from the wrist.

```ts
export function hand(o: HandOpts): Layer
```

A camera lens seen from the front: barrel, glass with a reflection, and an iris of blades that can open.

```ts
export function lens(o: LensOpts): LensPart
```
`lens({ id: "lens", pos: [960, 540], size: 360, open: { tl, at: 0.5, sfx: "click" } })`.

## `components/montage`

A run of short shots, each a word over a field, with the start/overlap arithmetic done for you. A shot's `start` is the leading edge of its incoming transition, so each shot is sized to hold `hold` seconds fully in view between the transition into it and the transition out.

```ts
export function montage(o: MontageOpts): Montage
```
`film.timeline({ shots: [...intro, ...montage({ items: [{ word: "fast", field: "#FF5A1F" }, ...], hold: 0.5 }).shots] })`.

## `components/promptBox`

A glass prompt card with a typed command: mono text, a caret that follows the typed end and blinks on beats, a `type` sound per character and an optional Enter (the card presses on a spring; the caret becomes a dot you can swell).

```ts
export function promptBox(o: PromptBoxOpts): Part
```
`promptBox({ tl, text: "turbomotion render launch.ts", at: 0.9, cps: 14, enterAt: 3.2 })`.

## `components/scribble`

A hand-drawn strike-through: a jittered zigzag path drawn on with `trim`, with a `glitch` on the first stroke.

```ts
export function scribble(o: ScribbleOpts): Part
```
`scribble({ tl, at: 1.2, pos: [960, 560], w: 1300, h: 760 })`: `shape` is the layer; the path overshoots the box slightly.

A big number that counts up and slams: it lands with a scale overshoot and a `stamp`, a small mono label under it.

```ts
export function statCounter(o: StatCounterOpts): Part
```
`statCounter({ tl, value: 373, suffix: " fps", label: "frames per second", at: 36 })`.

## `components/swarm`

A swarm of cubes that burst out of a point and tumble toward the lens, or drift in calmly.

```ts
export function swarm(o: SwarmOpts): SwarmPart
```
`swarm({ tl, id: "a", n: 9, seed: 3, at: 1.1, dur: 0.8, art: (i, s) => icon(names[i % 4], s * 0.7) })`.

## `components/textStack`

A stack of words that arrive on cue and lay themselves out. Rows grow downward (or upward from a bottom edge), a row that gets too wide wraps, and a centred row re-centres as words join it. Every position comes from the renderer's own text shaping, and words already on screen glide to their new place (a FLIP reflow) instead of jumping.

```ts
export interface StackRole
```
How one kind of word looks and enters.

```ts
export interface TextStackOpts
```
Options for `textStack`: lines of text that reflow (FLIP) as items are added, removed or reordered.

```ts
export function textStack(o: TextStackOpts): Part
```
`textStack({ tl, items, roles, pos: [90, 120], width: 560 })`. Returns the word layers in `words` (item order).

## `components/title3d`

A 3D word that tumbles in letter by letter: `letters3d` plus the launch film's entrance (stagger, back.out) as one call.

```ts
export function title3d(word: string, o: Title3DOpts): Part
```
`title3d("MOTION", { tl, at: 0.3, size: 240 })`: `letters` are the layers, `end` is when the last one has landed.

## `components/util`

Shared by the components: the default look (the launch film's tokens), the mono glyph width and a few helpers.

```ts
export interface Part
```
What every component returns: its layers (drop it straight into `shot({ layers })`), when it finishes, plus named parts.

```ts
export const THEME: Theme =
```
The defaults match `launch/design.ts`; pass `theme` to a component to restyle it.

```ts
export const MONO_ADVANCE = 0.6;
```
JetBrains Mono (and most monospace faces) advance 0.6 em per character.

```ts
export const monoWidth = (n: number, size: number): number
```
Width in pixels of `n` mono characters at `size`.

```ts
export function alpha(hex: string, a: number): string
```
`#rrggbb` plus an alpha 0..1 as `#rrggbbaa`.

```ts
export const shadow = (blur = 40, dy = 24, opacity = 0.2, color: [number, number, number] = [11, 12, 16]): Record<string, unknown> =>
```
A drop shadow effect.

```ts
export function mergeProps(where: string, ...parts: Array<Record<string, unknown>>): Record<string, unknown>
```
Merge prop objects into one, and THROW when two of them set the same key. Object spread keeps the last writer and drops the others without a word, which is how two idle motions on one `rotation` used to cancel each other.

## `components/waveform`

A row of thin rounded bars that grow in and then pulse like an audio level, driven by expressions (sines plus the beat).

```ts
export function waveform(o: WaveformOpts): Part
```
`waveform({ tl, at: 4.5, pos: [0, 200], w: 700, h: 90, parent: preview })`: one layer per bar, anchored on the baseline.

## `dimension`

A property that can be one number or a list of them (`scale: 2` or `scale: [2, 1]`) must have one shape on every key. A scalar tween against a per-axis value is read as "the same on every axis", so the two always merge.

```ts
export function matchAxes(prop: string, tweens: Tween[], base: Val | undefined, id: string): { tweens: Tween[]; base: Val | undefined }
```
`base` and the tweens of `prop` with every value written for the same number of axes.

## `film-types`

```ts
export interface Hit
```
A sound on a moment. `at` is film time (a number, or a literal like `"title.start+0.8"`); inside `shot({ hits })` it is shot-local seconds.

```ts
export interface ColorOpts
```
The `color` option of a composition: see `CompOpts.color`.

## `image-check`

`image()` options, checked where the author wrote them instead of by the engine's schema error at render time.

```ts
export function checkImage(src: string, o: ImageOpts): string
```
Throws a message naming the option and the fix; returns `src` so it can be used inline.

## `item-tweens`

Tweening the items of a shape layer: `tl.to(ring, { items: { 0: { trim_end: 1, stroke_width: 6 } } })`. The engine animates an item's trim, offset, rotation, scale, opacity, stroke and fill; a rect's size and corner radius are plain numbers in the schema, so animate the item's `scale` (about its `anchor`) instead.

```ts
export const itemKey = (index: number | string, name: string): string
```
The tween key for item `index`'s property: `items.2.trim_end`.

```ts
export function flattenItems(items: unknown, where: string): Record<string, Val>
```
Flatten `{ 0: { trim_end: 1 } }` into `{ "items.0.trim_end": 1 }`, rejecting what the schema cannot animate.

```ts
export function itemBase(out: Record<string, any>, key: string, id: string): Val | undefined
```
What item `key` holds now in the layer JSON (`out.items`), or its resting value; undefined when it has neither.

```ts
export function setItem(out: Record<string, any>, key: string, value: unknown): void
```
Write `value` at the item property, copying along the way so the layer's own items stay untouched.

## `layer-motion-types`

Layer-level engine objects that are not keyframes: position wrapping, stagger, flip, motion along a path, floor reflection (crates/comp/src/schema/mod.rs). Everything here is on `LayerOpts`.

```ts
export interface Wrap
```
After the position is evaluated, wrap `x` and/or `y` into `[min, max)`: a ticker is `pos: ["time * -80", 900]` with `wrap: { x: [-1920, 1920] }`.

```ts
export interface LayerStagger
```
Direct children start `each` seconds apart.

```ts
export interface Flip
```
This layer flies from `from`'s transform onto its own, starting at `at`.

```ts
export interface Along
```
The layer's position follows an outline as `t` goes 0 to 1.

```ts
export interface Reflect
```
A faded, softened mirror of the layer on the floor beneath it.

## `layers`

Layers as builders. A layer holds its static properties and the tweens a timeline attached to it; `toJSON()` turns both into one composition layer.

```ts
export class Layer
```
A layer of any kind as a builder: its properties plus the tweens a timeline attached to it.

```ts
export function list(items: unknown, where = "layers"): Layer[]
```
The top-level layers in `items` (arrays are opened; groups stay whole).

```ts
export const flatten = (items: unknown, where = "layers"): Layer[]
```
Every layer in `items`, groups opened so children follow their parent.

```ts
export const text = (content: string | CounterSpec, o: TextOpts = {}): Layer
```
A text layer: `text("Hello", { size, font, weight, color, pos, preset })`. Also takes a counter `{ from, to, dur }`.

```ts example
import { comp, text } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(
  text("Hello", { id: "title", size: 160, weight: 800, color: "#ffffff", align: "center", pos: [960, 440], preset: { name: "rise", at: 0.2 } }),
  text({ from: 0, to: 100, dur: 1.5, suffix: "%" }, { id: "count", size: 120, color: "#ffd166", align: "center", pos: [960, 680] }),
);
export default film;
```

```ts
export const solid = (color: Color, o: SolidOpts = {}): Layer
```
A flat rectangle: backgrounds, flashes, mattes.

```ts example
import { comp, solid, text } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(
  solid("#2a4d9b", { id: "card", size: [960, 540], pos: [960, 540] }),
  text("Card", { id: "label", size: 140, weight: 800, color: "#ffffff", align: "center", pos: [960, 540] }),
);
export default film;
```

```ts
export const texture = (shader: string, o: TextureOpts = {}): Layer
```
A generator shader painted over the whole layer: a noise field, a gradient, grain, or your own `effects/<name>.sksl` with `@kind generator`. `turbomotion comp fx list` shows each generator's parameters (`params`).

```ts example
import { comp, texture, text } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(
  texture("noise", { id: "plate", size: [1920, 1080], pos: [960, 540], opacity: 0.5 }),
  text("Plate", { size: 160, color: "#ffffff", align: "center", pos: [960, 540] }),
);
export default film;
```

```ts
export const image = (src: string, o: ImageOpts = {}): Layer
```
A picture: `image("photo.jpg", { fit, focus, camera, parallax })`.

```ts example
import { comp, image } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(image("photo.jpg", { id: "photo", fit: "cover", camera: { from: { zoom: 1 }, to: { zoom: 1.15 }, dur: 3 } }));
export default film;
```

```ts
export const shape = (items: ShapeItem[], o: ShapeOpts = {}): Layer
```
A vector shape from raw items: `{rect: [x, y, w, h], radius, fill, stroke}`, `{ellipse: [...]}`, `{d: "M..."}`.

```ts example
import { comp, shape } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(shape(
  [{ ellipse: [0, 0, 200, 200], fill: "#ff5a1f" }, { rect: [-300, 240, 600, 16], fill: "#ffffff" }],
  { id: "badge", pos: [960, 440] },
));
export default film;
```

```ts
export function rect(w: number, h: number, o: RectOpts = {}): Layer
```
A rectangle centred on its position, optionally rounded: `rect(260, 340, { fill: "#ff6b3d", radius: 18 })`.

```ts example
import { comp, rect } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(rect(260, 340, { id: "card", fill: "#ff6b3d", radius: 18, pos: [960, 540] }));
export default film;
```

```ts
export function group(o: LayerOpts = {}, children: unknown = []): Layer
```
An invisible handle: parent layers to it to move, scale or rotate them as one.

```ts example
import { comp, group, rect } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(group({ id: "rig", pos: [960, 540] }, [
  rect(300, 300, { id: "left", fill: "#ff6b3d", pos: [-200, 0] }),
  rect(300, 300, { id: "right", fill: "#3d6bff", pos: [200, 0] }),
]));
export default film;
```

```ts
export const camera = (o: CameraOpts = {}): Layer
```
A 3D camera: `camera({ pos, poi, zoom, dof })`. Shots with 3D layers and no camera get a default one.

```ts example
import { comp, box, camera } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(
  box({ size: 300 }, { id: "cube", color: "#e8402f", pos: [960, 540, 0], rotation: [20, 30, 0] }),
  camera({ id: "cam", pos: [960, 540, -1800], poi: [960, 540, 0] }),
);
export default film;
```

```ts
export const light = (o: LightOpts): Layer
```
A light that shades every `three_d` layer: `light({ kind: "point", pos, color, intensity, radius })`; kinds are ambient, point, directional and spot.

```ts example
import { comp, box, camera, light } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(
  light({ id: "key", kind: "point", pos: [400, 200, -500], color: "#ffd9a0", intensity: 1.2, radius: 1400 }),
  box({ size: 300 }, { id: "cube", color: "#e8402f", pos: [960, 540, 0], rotation: [20, 30, 0] }),
  camera({ id: "cam", pos: [960, 540, -1800], poi: [960, 540, 0] }),
);
export default film;
```

```ts
export const raw = (spec: RawSpec): Layer
```
Escape hatch: any layer the engine knows, as written in `turbomotion comp catalogue`.

```ts example
import { comp, raw, solid } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(
  solid("#2a4d9b", { id: "plate" }),
  raw({ type: "adjustment", id: "grade", fx: [{ effect: "vignette" }] }),
);
export default film;
```

## `matte-check`

An adjustment layer applies to what is below it, limited by its own `masks`. The engine does not read a `matte` on an adjustment layer, and a matte source that is hidden is drawn nowhere, so such a film would apply the adjustment to the whole frame without saying so. Refuse it where the film is written, naming the layers.

```ts
export function checkAdjustmentMattes(layers: Layer[], where: string): void
```
Throw when an adjustment layer takes a matte from a layer in the same list that is `hidden`.

## `measure`

Layout with the exact font shaping used by the composition renderer.

```ts
export interface SourceRect { left: number; top: number; width: number; height: number }
```
`sourceRectAtTime`'s rectangle: top-left corner and size, px from the text block's top-left.

```ts
export interface TextBounds
```
Where the characters are: the same measurement a text layer's `box` and `comp inspect` use.

```ts
export function configureMeasure(roles: Record<string, string> = {}, directory = ""): void
```
Called by comp() so font roles and relative files agree with the film.

```ts
export function measure(text: string, options: MeasureOptions = {}): Measured
```
Pixel dimensions and character/word boxes, using the most recently constructed comp's fonts.

```ts
export const filmRoot = (): string
```
The asset root the latest comp() declared (relative to the script's folder).

## `motion`

Small deterministic helpers: seeded random numbers, ranges, interpolation, grids.

```ts
export function rand(seed: number): Rand
```
A seeded generator (mulberry32). The same seed always gives the same numbers, on every machine.

```ts
export function grid(cols: number, rows: number, cell: number | [number, number]): Cell[]
```
`cols` x `rows` cells of size `cell` (a number, or [width, height]), row by row, centred on the origin.

```ts
export function darken(color: string, amount = 0.55): string
```
Darken a `#rrggbb` colour by `amount` (0..1); other colour forms come back unchanged.

## `motion-path`

Writing motion paths and handles: checks what the engine would refuse, here, at the line that wrote it.

```ts
export function motionPath(keys: Array<PathKey | RovingKey>, opts: { spatial?: "auto" | "linear" | "bezier"; auto_orient?: boolean; loop?: MotionPath["loop"] } = {}): MotionPath
```
A position that follows a curve through its keys, with After Effects' keyframe handles. Keys at a time are `{ t, v }`; a key `{ roving: true, v }` has no time and keeps the speed even between the keys around it.

```ts example
import { comp, solid, motionPath } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#10131c" });
film.add(solid("#ffd166", { size: [120, 120], pos: motionPath([
  { t: 0, v: [300, 800], ease_out: "easy" },
  { roving: true, v: [900, 200] },
  { t: 3, v: [1600, 800], ease_in: "easy" },
], { auto_orient: true }) }));
export default film;
```

```ts
export function checkHandles(h: Handles, at: string): Handles
```
The checked handles of a tween (`ease_out` of its first key, `ease_in` of its last).

```ts
export function pathPos(tw: Tween, local: (t: number)
```
`tl.to(layer, { path })` as the layer's `pos`: the first point at the tween's start, the last at its end, the points between roving.

```ts
export function takePath(out: Record<string, any>, tweens: Tween[], local: (t: number)
```
Moves the `path` tween of a layer into its `pos`, and returns the other tweens. A path replaces the layer's own position, so a layer with a path tween takes no x/y/z tween and has no `pos` of its own to start from.

```ts
export function applyHandles(keys: Array<any>, h: Handles): void
```
Gives the last tween written into `keys` its handles: the key it starts from leaves with `out`, the key it ends on arrives with `in`. The named ease the end key carried is the one the handles replace.

## `motion-types`

Keyframe handles and motion paths: the types of After Effects' temporal and spatial interpolation, as the engine reads them (crates/comp/src/anim/prop). Everything here is also spelled in JSON; `motionPath` and `tl.to(layer, { path })` write it for you.

```ts
export type Handle = { speed: number | number[]; influence: number };
```
How a value leaves or arrives at a key, as After Effects' Keyframe Velocity dialog names it. Influence is a percent, 0 to 100.

```ts
export type Side = "linear" | "hold" | "auto" | "easy" | Handle;
```
One side of a key. `"linear"` keeps the segment's own speed, `"auto"` takes the slope between the neighbouring keys, `"easy"` is Easy Ease (speed 0, influence 33.33 %), `"hold"` (leaving only) keeps the value until the next key.

```ts
export interface PathHandles
```
Where a key's motion path bends. `in` points back along the path, `out` forward, both as offsets from the key.

```ts
export interface PathKey extends PathHandles
```
A key of a motion path, at a time. `ease` is the ease of the move INTO it; `ease_in` / `ease_out` replace it with speed and influence.

```ts
export interface RovingKey extends PathHandles
```
A key without a time: its place on the path is kept, and its time is found so the speed stays even between the fixed keys around it.

```ts
export interface MotionPath
```
A position that follows a curve: `pos: motionPath([...])`.

```ts
export interface HandleKey<V = number>
```
A key of a scalar or vector property that carries handles.

```ts
export type PathPoint = Vec2 | Vec3 | ({ v: Vec2 | Vec3 } & PathHandles);
```
A point of `tl.to(layer, { path })`: a place, or a place with the handles of the curve there.

```ts
export interface Handles
```
The two ends of a tween as speed and influence; they take the place of `ease`.

## `overwrite`

Interrupted properties retain their exact easing via the engine's scalar expression form.

```ts
export function overwritten(tweens: Tween[], base: Value | undefined, id: string, prop: string, local: LayerTime): unknown
```
Segment times are on the timeline's clock; the expressions it writes use the layer's own time (`local`).

## `raw-types`

The two builders that take the engine's own vocabulary: `texture` (a generator and its parameters) and `raw` (any layer type).

```ts
export type TextureParam = number | string | Color | Vec2 | { [key: string]: unknown };
```
One generator parameter, as `turbomotion comp fx list` shows it: a number, a colour or a name (a choice), a point, or an animated property.

```ts
export interface TextureOpts extends LayerOpts
```
What a `texture` layer takes besides the layer options: the generator's `params` and the size it paints.

```ts
export interface RawSpec
```
Any layer the engine knows, as `turbomotion comp catalogue layer <type>` prints it: `type` plus that type's keys.

## `relative`

Relative tween values: `"+=40"` means 40 more than where the property is when the tween starts.

```ts
export function relative(v: Val, cur: Val | undefined, where: string): Val
```
Resolve `"+=n"` / `"-=n"` (alone or per component of a vector) against `cur`; other values pass through.

## `shape-types`

Shape layers: the items a `shape([...])` takes, as the engine reads them (crates/comp/src/schema/shape.rs and path.rs). An item is one geometry plus how it is painted; `trim`, `offset`, `rotation`, `scale` and `opacity` can be tweened.

```ts
export interface PathGeometry
```
Exactly one of `d`, `points`, `rect`, `ellipse`, `polygon`, `star` names the outline; the rest refine it.

```ts
export type ItemFill = Color | "metal" | { color?: Color; gradient?: GradientFill; metal?: boolean | { highlight?: Color; mid?: Color; shadow?: Color }; opacity?: Prop; rule?: "nonzero" | "evenodd" };
```
A bare colour, `"metal"`, or one of `color`, `gradient`, `metal` with an `opacity` and a winding `rule`.

```ts
export interface ItemTrim
```
Draw only the part of the outline between `start` and `end` (0..1), shifted by `offset`: animate `end` to draw on.

```ts
export interface ItemPaint extends Omit<PathGeometry, GeometryKey>
```
How an item is refined and painted. A stroke is `stroke: { color, width }`, a fill is `fill`; there is no `stroke_width` here.

```ts
export type ShapeItem = OneOutline & ItemPaint;
```
One piece of a `shape()`: one outline plus how it is painted, e.g. `{ ellipse: [0, 0, 80, 50], fill: "#fff", stroke: { color: "#000", width: 4 } }`.

## `site`

Where in the author's script something was created, for errors found later (a tween merged at write-out, a layer the engine rejects). `sdk check` turns tracking on; otherwise nothing is recorded.

```ts
export function callSite(): string
```
The first stack frame outside the SDK: the line of the author's script that made this call.

```ts
export function noteSite(id: string): void
```
Remember the line that created layer `id` (only while the host asked for it).

## `sound`

Sound: audio layers, and hits (sound-kit cues placed on moments). Hits made on a timeline are shot-local seconds; `film.timeline` turns them into the engine's `"<shotId>.start+<t>"` literal, so the engine, which knows where each shot really starts once transitions overlap, puts them on the right frame.  The kit (`comp catalogue` -> `sound_kit`) has ~230 synthesised sounds in families. A cue names one of them: "whoosh"            any whoosh; the engine uses a different one each time (and a touch of pitch and gain) "whoosh/airy"       one of the airy whooshes        "whoosh/airy-01"   exactly that file "pluck/C4"          a pitched voice at a note (pluck, bell, marimba, stab, bass) `melody` and `drumPattern` turn a list of notes or a step pattern into hits, so a bed can be sequenced from kit voices.

```ts
export function audio(src: string, o: AudioOpts = {}): Layer
```
A sound on the timeline: `audio("launch/music/bed.wav", { id: "music", volume: 0.8, fade_out: 1 })`.

```ts
export const hit = (at: number | string, cue: string, volume?: number): Hit
```
A hit at film time: `hit(26, "boom")`, `hit("drop.start+0.2", "riser/quick", 0.5)`, `hit(3, "pluck/C4")`. A family name ("whoosh", "kick", "ui") varies on its own: neighbouring hits of the same cue get different sounds.

```ts
export function inShot(id: string, hits: Hit[] = []): Hit[]
```
Shot-local hits as film-time literals: `at: 0.8` in shot "deep" becomes `"deep.start+0.8"`.

```ts
export type Step = string | string[] | null | number | { note: string | string[]; volume?: number };
```
One step of a melody: a note, several notes at once (a chord), or a rest (`null`, `"."`, `"-"`, `0`).

```ts
export const transpose = (note: string, semitones: number): string
```
`transpose("C4", 7)` is `"G4"`.

```ts
export function scale(root: string, mode: "major" | "minor" | "major-pentatonic" | "minor-pentatonic" | "chromatic" = "major", octaves = 1): string[]
```
The notes of a scale from `root` ("C3") upward: `scale("C3", "minor", 2)` is two octaves of C minor, ending on the top root.

```ts
export function melody(notes: Step[], o: MelodyOpts): Hit[]
```
A tune from a kit voice: `melody(["C4", "Eb4", "G4", null, "C5"], { at: 2, step: 0.25, voice: "pluck" })` emits one hit per note (`pluck/C4` ...). Rests are `null`; an array is a chord. Notes outside the voice's two octaves are reported by the engine.

```ts
export function drumPattern(pattern: string, o: DrumOpts): Hit[]
```
Hits from a step pattern: `drumPattern("x...x...x...x.x.", { at: 4, bpm: 120, voice: "kick" })`. `x` hits, `X` accents, `o` is a soft hit (half volume), `.`, `-` and spaces rest, `|` is a bar line (ignored). Use a map for several drums at once. Use one call per drum so each line reads like a row in a drum machine.

## `stage`

Smart animate. Describe where each named layer sits in a few poses, then glide between poses: the layers are matched by name, only the properties that differ are tweened, and every layer lands on the same clock. This is what makes a scene feel like one object changing rather than one picture replacing another.  const s = stage({ title, clock }, { start: { title: { x: 360, y: 300, opacity: 0 }, clock: { x: 360, y: 800, scale: 0.6 } }, shown: { title: { opacity: 1 }, clock: { y: 640, scale: 1 } }, }).start("start"); s.go(tl, "shown", { at: 0.4, dur: 0.7, ease: "expo.out", stagger: 0.06 });  A layer a pose does not mention keeps its place. To make one disappear, give it `opacity: 0`. A group's opacity reaches everything parented to it (the engine's null layers do not pass opacity down, so the stage does).

```ts
export interface Pose
```
The properties a pose can set; the same names `tl.to` animates.

```ts
export class Stage
```
Named poses for layers; `go` tweens between them.

```ts
export const stage = (layers: Record<string, Layer>, poses: Record<string, Record<string, Pose>>): Stage
```
Smart Animate: name poses for a set of layers, then `go("pose", { at, dur })` moves every layer to its new state.

## `text-fx`

Text effects that need more than a few options: type on a path, wrapped on a surface, scrolling rows, flipping letters, cipher decode. Each returns plain engine JSON, typed in ./types.

```ts
export const textOnPath = (content: string, path: TextPathOpts, o: TextOpts = {}): Layer
```
Text along any path (After Effects' Path Options): `textOnPath("HELLO", { ellipse: [0, 0, 300, 300] }, { pos: [960, 540] })`. The path is in pixels from the layer's `pos`. Characters advance by arc length and turn to the tangent; `align` picks which end of the text sits at `first_margin` (left), the middle, or `last_margin` (right). Characters pushed past an open path's ends hide.

```ts
export function orbitText(content: string, radius: number, lap: Seconds, o: TextOpts = {}): Layer
```
Text circling a point: one exact lap every `lap` seconds, forever (the lap is `travel` 0 to 1 on a closed path, so the loop has no seam). `orbitText("SPIN ", 300, 6, { pos: [960, 540], size: 60 })`. A negative `lap` goes the other way round.

```ts example
import { comp, orbitText } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(orbitText("SPIN ", 300, 6, { id: "ring", pos: [960, 540], size: 60, color: "#ffffff" }));
export default film;
```

```ts
export const wrapText = (content: string, kind: "cylinder" | "sphere", o: TextOpts & { radius?: TextSurfaceOpts["radius"]; turn?: TextSurfaceOpts["turn"]; back?: boolean } = {}): Layer
```
Text wrapped on a cylinder or sphere (the CC Cylinder / CC Sphere look, with live type): `wrapText("WORLD TOUR", "cylinder", { pos: [960, 540] })`. Each character stands on the surface and turns with it; `turn` (degrees, animatable) scrolls the text round, characters facing away hide unless `back` is set. The surface's axis goes through `pos` and the vanishing point is `pos`.

```ts
export const marquee = (content: string, m: MarqueeOpts, o: TextOpts = {}): Layer
```
A seamlessly repeating, scrolling row (ticker, marquee). The text and `gap` form one period; copies are laid end to end across the frame and shifted by `speed` px/s. Left aligned from `pos`, so put the layer at x 0 for a full-width row.

```ts
export function charFlip(o: { axis?: "x" | "y"; from?: number; each?: Seconds; at?: Seconds; dur?: Seconds; z?: number; by?: "chars" | "words" } = {}): TextAnimator
```
Letters flip in one by one (After Effects' per-character 3D): turn about `axis` from `from` degrees to flat, `each` seconds apart.

```ts
export function decode(o: { charset?: CipherCharset; each?: Seconds; at?: Seconds; dur?: Seconds; rate?: number; seed?: number } = {}): TextAnimator
```
Cipher decode: characters show random noise, then lock on to the real ones left to right, `each` seconds apart. Deterministic by `seed`. `charset` is a name (`auto`, `upper`, `lower`, `digits`, `alnum`, `hex`, `binary`, `symbols`, `matrix`) or the characters themselves.

```ts
export const outlineText = (content: string, o: TextOpts & { stroke_color?: Color; width?: number; at?: Seconds; dur?: Seconds } = {}): Layer
```
Outline-only type that writes itself on: stroked glyph outlines from 0 to 1 of their length over `dur` seconds.

## `three`

Solids. Every 3D object is one `mesh` layer whose `geometry` says what it is made of: glyph outlines, a box, a sphere, a torus, a cylinder or an SVG path pushed into depth. `text3d` and `letters3d` are the text geometry; `spin` turns any of them about its own axis.

```ts
export function mesh(geometry: Geometry, o: MeshOpts = {}): Layer
```
A mesh from any geometry: `mesh({ kind: "sphere", size: 300 }, { color: "#e8402f", pos: [960, 540, 0] })`.

```ts
export const box = (g: Omit<BoxGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
A box: `box({ size, height?, depth? }, { color, side, pos, rotation })`.

```ts example
import { comp, box, camera } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(
  box({ size: 300 }, { id: "cube", color: "#e8402f", pos: [960, 540, 0], rotation: [20, 30, 0] }),
  camera({ id: "cam", pos: [960, 540, -1800], poi: [960, 540, 0] }),
);
export default film;
```

```ts
export const sphere = (g: Omit<SphereGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
A sphere of diameter `size`.

```ts
export const torus = (g: Omit<TorusGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
A ring facing the viewer: outer diameter `size`, band thickness `tube`.

```ts
export const cylinder = (g: Omit<CylinderGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
A cylinder of diameter `size` and `height`; `top: 0` makes a cone.

```ts
export const extrude = (g: Omit<ExtrudeGeometry, "kind">, o?: MeshOpts): Layer
```
An SVG path `d` filled and pushed `depth` deep.

```ts
export function text3d(content: string, o: Text3DOpts = {}): Layer
```
Extruded text: `text3d("Hi", { font, weight, size, depth, bevel, color, side, material, ...layer })`.

```ts example
import { comp, camera, text3d } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(
  text3d("Hi", { id: "word", size: 300, weight: 800, depth: 60, bevel: 6, color: "#ffd166", side: "#c2410c", pos: [960, 540, 0], rotation: [20, 20, 0] }),
  camera({ id: "cam", pos: [960, 540, -1800], poi: [960, 540, 0] }),
);
export default film;
```

```ts
export function letters3d(word: string, o: Letters3DOpts = {}): Layer[]
```
Split `word` into one 3D text layer per letter, centred on `pos` (default the origin: pass your own). Letter boxes come from the renderer's own shaping (`measure`), so kerning and tracking match flat text. Spaces take room but make no layer. Returns the layers in reading order, ready for a staggered tween.

```ts example
import { comp, camera, letters3d } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
film.add(
  ...letters3d("MOVE", { id: "m", pos: [960, 540, 0], size: 260, depth: 50, color: "#ffd166", side: "#c2410c", rotation: [15, 20, 0] }),
  camera({ id: "cam", pos: [960, 540, -1800], poi: [960, 540, 0] }),
);
export default film;
```

```ts
export function spin(degreesPerSecond: number, from = 0): string
```
A turntable: the angle of a steady turn as an expression, for the Z Rotation of a 3D object (`rotation`), or any of the three axes (`rotation: [0, spin(90), 0]`). `box({ size: 200 }, { rotation: spin(90) })` makes a full turn in four seconds; `from` is the starting angle.

## `timeline`

A GSAP-style timeline. `tl.to(layer, { rotation: [null, 90, null], duration: 0.8 }, 0.2)` records tweens on the layer; when the layer is written out (compile.ts), all tweens on one property merge into one key list in time order. Every position on a timeline is the clock of the shot (or comp) the layers live in, whatever a layer's own `start` is.

```ts
export class Timeline
```
Tweens placed on a time axis, compiled into each layer's keyframes.

```ts
export const timeline = (defaults: { ease?: Ease; duration?: Seconds } = {}): Timeline
```
A GSAP-style timeline: `tl.to(layer, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.5 }, at)`, `from`, `set`, with `stagger` and `overwrite`.

```ts example
import { comp, text, timeline } from "turbomotion";
const film = comp({ width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 30, dur: 3, bg: "#1a1d29" });
const title = text("Slide", { id: "title", size: 160, weight: 800, color: "#ffffff", align: "center", pos: [960, 540] });
const tl = timeline({ ease: "power2.out" });
tl.from(title, { opacity: 0, x: -200, duration: 0.8 }, 0.2);
film.add(title);
export default film;
```

## `tween-types`

```ts
export type Num = number | `+=${number}` | `-=${number}`;
```
A number, or one relative to the property when the tween starts: `"+=40"`, `"-=0.5"`.

```ts
export interface ItemVars
```
What an item of a shape layer lets a tween change (`tl.to(layer, { items: { 0: { trim_end: 1 } } })`). A rect's size and radius are fixed; animate `scale` instead.

```ts
export interface Animatable
```
Properties a tween can animate. `x`/`y`/`z` move `pos`; `pos: [x, y, z]` moves several at once.

## `types`

Shared types. Everything an author can write is described here, so an editor catches mistakes before the render does.

```ts
export type Prop<T = number> = T | string | { [key: string]: unknown };
```
A property: a constant, an expression string, or any raw form the engine accepts (tween, keys, loop).

```ts
export interface Material
```
How a lit 3D layer answers to light.

```ts
export interface Transit
```
A named entrance or exit of the layer as a whole. Its times are in the layer's own clock (they start at the layer's `start`).

```ts
export type Lit = boolean;
```
A 3D layer is lit when the composition has lights; `false` keeps it flat.

```ts
export interface LayerOpts
```
What every layer takes. `x`, `y`, `z` are shorthand for `pos`.

```ts
export interface TextBox
```
A rectangle fitted to the characters showing: a text bar, pill, chip or lower third. Drawn behind the glyphs, in the layer's own pixels.

```ts
export interface TextUnitProps
```
What a text animator does to a unit at full weight. Rotations share the layer's `rotation: [x, y, z]` axes and signs.

```ts
export interface TextWiggle
```
A random factor per unit (`min` 0, `max` 1; either may be negative). `rate` 0 keeps each unit's factor, above 0 it drifts, that many new targets a second.

```ts
export type CipherCharset = "auto" | "upper" | "lower" | "digits" | "alnum" | "hex" | "binary" | "symbols" | "matrix" | (string & {});
```
Where a cipher's random characters come from: a name, or any string of characters.

```ts
export interface TextPathOpts
```
Text along a path. Exactly one geometry (`d`, `points`, `ellipse`, `rect`, `polygon`, `star`) or `layer`.

```ts
export interface CounterSpec
```
`text` may also be a counter that counts from `from` to `to`.

```ts
export interface Framing
```
One end of an image's Ken Burns move: `zoom` 1 is the fitted image; `center` is a fraction of the image.

```ts
export interface TorusGeometry { kind: "torus"; size: number; tube?: number }
```
A ring facing the viewer: `size` is the outer diameter, `tube` the band's thickness (a quarter of `size`).

```ts
export interface CylinderGeometry { kind: "cylinder"; size: number; height: number; top?: number }
```
`top` is the top diameter (0 makes a cone).

```ts
export interface ExtrudeGeometry { kind: "extrude"; d: string; size: number; depth?: number; bevel?: number }
```
An SVG path `d` (filled) scaled to `size` wide and pushed `depth` deep (0.3 x size when left out).

## `vector-tweens`

The layer's three-dimensional vectors: After Effects' X, Y and Z Rotation, its X, Y and Z Orientation, and the point its face turns toward. The engine holds each as a vector of three components, so a tween of one of them becomes a tween per component, and the components are put back together when the layer is written out.

```ts
export const VECTORS: Record<string, number> = { rotation: 3, orientation: 3, aim: 3 };
```
The vector properties, and how many components each has.

```ts
export const vectorKey = (name: string, index: number): string
```
The tween key for component `index` of `name`: `rotation.1`.

```ts
export const isVectorKey = (key: string): boolean
```
Is this tween key one component of a vector property?

```ts
export const parseVectorKey = (key: string): { name: string; index: number }
```
The vector property and the component a tween key names.

```ts
export function flattenVector(name: string, value: unknown, where: string): Record<string, Val>
```
Split a vector tween into one entry per component. `rotation` is the one vector with a shorthand: a bare number is the Z Rotation, the turn in the layer's own plane. The other vectors are always a triple.

```ts
export function vectorBase(out: Record<string, any>, name: string, index: number, id: string): Val
```
The value component `index` of the vector `name` starts from.

```ts
export function vectorComponents(out: Record<string, any>, name: string): Array<number | string>
```
The components of the vector `name` as the layer holds them now: a lone number or expression is the last one (the Z Rotation), and an expression in an axis stays an expression instead of turning into 0.

```ts
export function setVector(out: Record<string, any>, name: string, parts: Map<number, unknown>): void
```
Write the tweened components of `name` back into the layer, keeping the components it does not touch.

```ts
export function fillVector(base: Array<number | string>, value: Array<number | string | null | undefined>): Array<number | string>
```
Fill the holes of a partial vector against the layer's current components: a hole leaves that axis alone.

```ts
export function checkVectors(out: Record<string, any>, id: string): void
```
The orientation and the point of interest are vectors of three; a mistake here is worth naming.
